newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen weakening on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen weakening on consolidation.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to consolidate on Thursday in reaction to recent steep rises but North Korea's war threat was seen fizzling out, brokers said.
They said the Kia Group's rumoured financial troubles would continue to dampen investor sentiment, despite a strong denial by the nation's eighth largest conglomerate.
"The market seemed to over-react to the North Korean issue. But the downward correction will continue," said Woo Sang-chul at Tongyang Securities.
The composite stock index closed on Wednesday 19.08 points lower at 773.21.

North Korea warned on Wednesday it was ready for a "final battle" with the U.S. and South Korea, which it accused of preparing to attack while the North was weakened by a dire food shortage. South Korea denied stepping up military exercises and Seoul officials accused North Korea of trying to justify its huge military spendings by whipping up war threats.
Brokers said large-capitalised shares would try to rebound but sustained upward movement looked unlikely. Smaller companies would remain weak on worries about margin loan calls, they said.
